name: signal-protocol-platform
description: Signal is a deterministic decision-protocol platform that provides a runtime for executing queries, mutations, and events through a typed, schema-validated envelope protocol. The system enforces idempotency, replay-safety, and auditability across all operations.

coreDomains.name: protocol
coreDomains.description: Pure contracts, type definitions, envelope schema, naming conventions, result/error models, and capability declarations.
coreDomains.intent: Define the wire contract that all operations must conform to.

coreDomains.name: runtime
coreDomains.description: Execution engine that dispatches queries, mutations, and events through a registry with idempotency, observability, and replay support.
coreDomains.intent: Provide the deterministic execution kernel for Signal operations.

coreDomains.name: decision
coreDomains.description: Decision reasoning module: evidence assessment, journaling, coherence checking, outcome feedback, learning, prediction, simulation, and stewardship governance.
coreDomains.intent: Enable structured, accountable decision-making with learning and governance.

coreDomains.name: commitment
coreDomains.description: Commitment evaluation module: trust scoring, constraint checking, resource allocation, and policy-based commitment recommendations.
coreDomains.intent: Evaluate and recommend commitment levels for decisions.

coreDomains.name: agency
coreDomains.description: Agency pipeline: action sizing, calibration, learning from traces, outcome resolution, policy evaluation, and self-diagnosis.
coreDomains.intent: Manage autonomous agency cycles with calibrated confidence.

coreDomains.name: kernel
coreDomains.description: Plugin architecture and pipeline orchestration: SignalPackage envelope, 4-stage pipeline (generate → analyze → decide → execute), event bus, state stores.
coreDomains.intent: Provide the immutable package contract and pipeline orchestration for signal processing.

transportBindings.description: In-process dispatcher for event pub/sub within the same Node.js process.

keyInvariants: All operations conform to the signal.v1 envelope protocol
Events are immutable facts safe to consume more than once
Results follow { ok: true, result } | { ok: false, error } pattern
No backward dependencies in the layer DAG
